Subject: Latency & streaming requirements — post-call recap and next actions

Hi Emma — thanks again for the demo call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned on the performance qualification scope.

Key takeaways from call:
- Target E2E p95 latency goal: in the ballpark of 150–250ms (you mentioned 200ms as ideal)
- Target E2E p99 latency: ≤350ms for interactive flows
- Concurrency: sustained 3k–5k concurrent users for the initial rollout; burst to 8k for marketing spikes
- Throughput: ~120 req/s (avg), spiky bursts up to ~600 req/s during peak minutes
- Streaming: first-token streaming is required for the primary chat experience — you called out desire for first-token under ~80ms once connection established

Open clarifying items we promised to follow up on:
1) Define precise measurement point for "E2E" (client RTT + gateway + Redwood runtime + model decode) — we want to ensure apples-to-apples with your current provider.
2) Confirm payload assumptions (avg tokens in/out, typical system prompt size, attachments or base64 payloads).
3) Provide a hosted POC runbook and a short test harness you can run from an internal agent to validate p95/p99.

Attached: a short CSV template (finapps_latency_template.csv) — please populate with sample request sizes and concurrency patterns if you can.

Next steps proposed:
- Emma & Eng team: populate CSV with 1 representative flow and one peak-flow by EOD Wednesday 6/10
- Redwood: we’ll send a hosted POC configuration and expected test harness commands by Thursday 6/11
- Align on measurement definitions (I'll loop David to confirm runtime vs network boundaries)

Thanks — and copying Aditya and David for SCC/SE follow-up.

Best,
Soojin Lee

Thanks Soojin — good write-up. Quick answers and a filled sample attached.

Numbers we confirmed on the call (to make explicit):
- E2E measurement point: client browser -> app gateway -> Redwood -> response back to app gateway -> client render. We need your guidance if you’ll provide SDK probes or we’ll measure from our side.
- p95 target: 200ms (hard target for conversational UI)
- p99 target: 350ms (we can tolerate small tail for long context)
- Sustained concurrency: 4,000 users (approx concurrent websocket connections across pods)
- Sustained throughput: 120 req/s average; peak sustained bursts up to 600 req/s for short windows (~1–2 minutes)
- Streaming requirement: First-token for streaming chat should be <80ms from server-side decode to first byte for the client (we will measure RT TTFB).

Attached: finapps_latency_template.csv — I filled one representative chat flow (avg 40 tokens in, 80 tokens out) and one peak flow (avg 12 tokens in, 30 tokens out, high freq).

We’d prefer Redwood-hosted POC if you can guarantee isolation for the tests. Timeline: we want a 2-week POC window starting as early as next Monday 6/15. Procurement for the POC is fast — we just need a service agreement + test account.

Also, can you confirm whether your p95/p99 numbers include cold-starts for new containers? We typically exclude cold-starts but need to be explicit.

Thanks,
Emma

Hi Emma — quick technical clarifications from SE to make sure the POC is configured to measure the same thing you care about.

Measurement & test config notes:
- "E2E" definition: we recommend both (A) client-side measurement you will run (real network path) and (B) server-side probe (from Redwood agent in same region) to separate network noise. We'll provide the agent to run within your VPC if you'd like.
- Cold starts: by default our hosted runtime keeps hot workers and uses continuous batching; for POC we can pin a "warm" profile that minimizes cold starts. For the SLA-style numbers, we exclude extreme cold-starts (i.e., container boot + model load) unless you want that included.
- Tokenization and payload size: please confirm whether attachments are base64 or passed as references — base64 will increase decode time nonlinearly.
- Streaming first-byte: streaming latency depends on both model latency (decode time to first token) and network tail. We can instrument server-side TTFB and stream in ~10ms chunks; to achieve <80ms server-side first-byte we recommend the following config: quantized model variant, pinned workers, and small batch windows (~4–8ms).

Suggested POC test harness we'll ship:
- A small load generator script (node/python) that replays your CSV flows from 3 geographic agents
- Server-side probe endpoint that returns per-request timings (gatewayRT, runtimeRT, decodeRT, ttfb)
- A short set of test knobs: concurrency, request size, model_variant, batching_window_ms

I’ll attach a short POC checklist (redwood_poc-checklist.pdf) and a sample command set.

If that all sounds good I’ll prepare the hosted config and credentials.

-David
